title: fix(worktrees): reserve capacity on PostgreSQL
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: PostgreSQL-backed worktree creation fails when reserving capacity because its upsert references an ambiguous `owner` column.

## User Impact

Managed Git worktrees can be created and registered on PostgreSQL. Reservation renewal still requires the same owner; a replacement owner remains protected. SQLite behavior and persisted schemas are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Qualify the target table's existing owner predicate. Allocation, leases, worker dispatch, and error propagation remain with their native owners. The new PostgreSQL suite is now included in the existing conformance runner's default targets and CI shards.

## Executed behavior evidence

The committed `capacity.postgres.test.ts` now calls **`ManagedWorktreeService.create`**, creates a real local Git repository, uses the real allocation/lease/capacity worker transport against **PostgreSQL 17.11**, reads the created checkout's `README.md`, and checks the persisted worktree registry. This case does not mock dispatch, database admission, SQL, Git, or filesystem effects. The suite owns teardown of its isolated database schemas, workers, state, and checkout.

The same final suite was executed twice, changing only the production conflict predicate for the negative control:

```text
Original predicate: .where("owner", "=", key)
FAIL creates and registers a real Git checkout through PostgreSQL-backed allocation
error: column reference "owner" is ambiguous (PostgreSQL 42702)
FAIL admits and renews only the current owner capacity reservation
error: column reference "owner" is ambiguous (PostgreSQL 42702)

Fixed predicate: .where("state_leases.owner", "=", key)
PASS creates and registers a real Git checkout through PostgreSQL-backed allocation — 1195 ms
PASS admits and renews only the current owner capacity reservation — 42 ms
Test Files 1 passed; Tests 2 passed
```

The second case separately proves renewal and refusal after reservation-owner replacement with real PostgreSQL; only that case substitutes the transport grant callback. Both cases failed for the intended SQL error on the control. Fixed source bytes were restored and verified afterward.

Reproduce with a disposable PostgreSQL database:

```sh
node scripts/test-database-conformance.mjs --engine postgres --list
node scripts/test-database-conformance.mjs --engine postgres --connection "$TEST_POSTGRES_URL" -- src/agents/worktrees/capacity.postgres.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

## Validation and limits

- Default conformance selection now includes this file. Existing target-inventory, disjoint-shard, listing, and argument-validation tests: **8 passed**. Their temporary fixture now declares its actual ESM package type instead of triggering an unexpected Node warning.
- Real PostgreSQL green run: **37.08 seconds wall**, including **29.7 seconds** of compiled-worker preparation; test bodies total about **1.24 seconds**. Negative control: **141.45 seconds wall**, including cold worker preparation. CI duration remains available on the current head's checks.
- Existing PostgreSQL/SQLite capacity sibling proof: **21 passed** on the original production fix; the production predicate is unchanged by this follow-up.
- Targeted agents-other and tooling test-type checks, typed lint (3 files), formatting, diff checks and staged test-line ratchet passed.
- Fresh installed independent P0–P2 autoreview of this complete candidate: **scoped-clean**, no findings.
- Full runtime/plugin/declaration build already passed with the original seven independent production fixes composed; this correction changes only regression selection, tests and allocation metadata. Current-head PR CI supplies broad proof.
- The **+85 test-line allocation** covers the two distinct PostgreSQL contracts and the one-line ESM fixture setup. The shared baseline is unchanged. No production API, schema, cache, or test-only seam is added.
- This is real production-owner/database/Git evidence, not a live cloud/model run. It makes no claim about worktree retirement: an exploratory `service.remove` call outside the CLI one-shot scope exposed a separate main-thread PostgreSQL admission refusal and was not included in the allocation claim.

## Public CLI → Gateway → PostgreSQL proof

Executed on 2026-11-04 against PR head 14674c64679e1adb0faf58bde27bd881d92759ba, not just ManagedWorktreeService integration. The normal pnpm openclaw launcher built and ran the production CLI and two disposable, authenticated loopback Gateways. Both installations used fresh owned HOME/config/state directories and separate databases on PostgreSQL 17.11, with database.engine=postgres and the documented OPENCLAW_DATABASE_DSN env SecretRef. No production dispatch, Git, lease, capacity, or worker transport was mocked. No test admission override was installed.

The project fixture was a clean checkout of the existing PR commit; no fixture source commit was needed. Default worktree acceleration was left enabled, including its normal internal template cache.

### Exact public entrypoint

With the respective isolated config/state/DSN and loopback port selected, the commands were as below. Each gateway run stayed in its own supervised foreground process; health and creation were separate CLI invocations.

```bash
pnpm openclaw --profile capacity-proof-red gateway run
pnpm openclaw --profile capacity-proof-red health --json
pnpm openclaw --profile capacity-proof-red worktrees create "$REPO"   --name capacity-public-red   --base-ref 14674c64679e1adb0faf58bde27bd881d92759ba --json

pnpm openclaw --profile capacity-proof-green gateway run
pnpm openclaw --profile capacity-proof-green health --json
pnpm openclaw --profile capacity-proof-green worktrees create "$REPO"   --name capacity-public-green   --base-ref 14674c64679e1adb0faf58bde27bd881d92759ba --json
```

**Red:** the same head with only the capacity predicate reverted from state_leases.owner to the original owner reference. Health passed; public creation exited1. The running Gateway recorded the worktrees.create RPC failing with:

```text
column reference "owner" is ambiguous: code=42702
```

The public list was empty, PostgreSQL contained zero worktree records, the requested checkout was absent, and no worktree leases remained. The uncertain-error receipt was reconciled before proceeding; no blind retry or offline fallback was used for creation.

**Green:** pristine 14674c64679e1adb0faf58bde27bd881d92759ba, rebuilt by the normal launcher. Health and public creation both exited0. The returned id f1067054-e076-463f-be04-4a0911776531 appeared in the public list and the real PostgreSQL worktrees row, with matching path, branch and base ref. The physical checkout had HEAD 14674c64679e1adb0faf58bde27bd881d92759ba, clean Git status, and README bytes matching the source (SHA256 368166ce96af9cf49729ef813f1ed5e93b04d26f7b3598c9c8721779d534cbda). No worktree leases remained after creation.

### Executing build binding

- Green native build: 2026.10.10-14674c64679e-2026-11-04T06-41-50.645Z; inputsClean=true.
- Green input signature: 59f1de5bc1851905aae4bc1c230680904ddafbd5b9e7ed817332e48e47b51046.
- Red input signature: 6cfe3aa07ce5ca33b9c4073e4212f410f7bfb57879120dfe04e58a5d1d959527; inputsClean=false solely for the one-line inverse patch.
- Both actual Gateway processes used the same pinned OpenClaw Bun binary, SHA256 0cef667e2f3fd465b6429904ed074381a679be379ec44fa42b5f460ed118b2b8. Serving process cwd, executable, build stamps and artifact hashes were captured.

### Cleanup and scope

Lossless cleanup correctly retained the unpushed synthetic branch. A separate online worktrees.remove --force RPC hit the PostgreSQL main-thread admission restriction; that issue was recorded, not hidden or patched into this change. After stopping the owned Gateway, the same public CLI in supported offline one-shot mode removed the checkout and retained its native safety snapshot/removal receipt. Verification found zero active PostgreSQL worktrees, no worktree leases, and the requested path absent. Both Gateways stopped cleanly; the PostgreSQL container and its anonymous volume were removed and all selected ports closed.

This is shipped CLI/Gateway entrypoint evidence for PostgreSQL worktree creation. It is not a live-model, cloud-provider, stress, or whole-lifecycle correctness claim. No PR/source code changes or extra test-policy changes were required for this proof.
